items.summary: President Donald Trump has chosen immigration hardliner Stephen Miller to serve as his new White House chief of staff. Miller steps into the powerful role as the administration navigates a difficult lame-duck period following the Republican loss of both houses of Congress. Throughout his career, Miller has been a prominent and controversial architect of hardline immigration policies and domestic initiatives.
items.why: As chief of staff, Miller's prominent policy influence shapes the administration's ongoing domestic agenda and political strategy.

items.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest following the collapse of a major U.S.-owned digital lender. The financial crisis left millions without access to their money and triggered widespread protests. Legislators unanimously found Peña guilty of malfeasance, and Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in to finish the term.
items.why: The abrupt political transition and banking crisis in Paraguay disrupt regional governance and highlight vulnerabilities in digital financial systems serving a large portion of the adult population.

items.title: NASA's Swift space observatory re-enters atmosphere after 22-year mission
items.original_title: APOD: 2026 November 6 – A Farewell to Swift
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 over North Sumatra, Indonesia, ending nearly 22 years of service. The satellite observed the universe's fastest and most energetic explosions using coordinated ultraviolet, optical, X-ray, and gamma-ray detectors. Decay of the spacecraft's orbit was accelerated by the recent solar maximum, and a planned orbital boost mission was unsuccessful.
items.why: Although the spacecraft has burned up, its collected multi-wavelength survey data will continue to serve astrophysical research on energetic transient events.
technical_details: The satellite operated Ultraviolet/Optical, X-ray, and gamma-ray telescopes together to study high-energy cosmic explosions.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: NASA's Swift space observatory re-enters atmosphere after 22-year mission

items.title: Testing Humanoid Cleaning Robots Reveals Current Technological Limits
items.original_title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: A journalist tested a commercial cleaning service using remotely piloted humanoid robots in San Francisco. While capable of performing physical tasks like vacuuming and mopping, the robots frequently stalled due to connectivity issues and required significant human oversight. Startups are using data collected from these supervised tasks to train future autonomous models.
items.why: Commercializing humanoid robots for everyday domestic chores remains challenging, and widespread deployment could eventually impact the livelihoods of human cleaners.
technical_details: Many tasks require kinematic guidance where human pilots perform motions that are transmitted to the robot.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Testing Humanoid Cleaning Robots Reveals Current Technological Limits

Officials stated that missile and drone production lines have been successfully transferred to these secure subterranean facilities.
